newsitem.title: SPAIN: SWIMMING-IRELAND'S OLYMPIC CHAMPION WINS EURO GOLD.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-IRELAND'S OLYMPIC CHAMPION WINS EURO GOLD.

text.p: Ireland's triple Olympic champion Michelle de Bruin resisted a bold challenge from a new 15-year-old rival to claim her first gold medal of the European swimming championships on Tuesday.
But she could be in trouble after missing an obligatory press conference following her win. Officials are to meet on Wednesday to decide whether to take any action against her.

De Bruin, now competing under her married name after swimming as Michelle Smith at the Atlanta Games, trailed European junior champion Yana Klochkova for much of the women's 400 metres individual medley but drew on her formidable power to pass the young Ukrainian on the last length.
"I'm very happy. Even if it's the first medal of many this week, the first is always the most difficult," the 27-year-old Irishwoman said.

De Bruin opened a lead on the initial butterfly leg but the Ukrainian hit back on the backstroke and pulled ahead on the breaststroke before the Olympic champion reeled her in down the last length of the 50-metre San Pablo pool.

De Bruin, whose astonishing late rise to the top after years among the back markers has been highly controversial, won by nearly a second in four minutes 42.08 seconds, almost three seconds slower than her winning 4:39.18 in Atlanta.
She collected her first two European titles at the last championships in Vienna in 1995 and is aiming for a staggering five this time.
Klochkova, who turned 15 only this month, was second in 4:43.07 and impressed Erik de Bruin, the Irish swimmer's husband and coach.
"She's very good. She's going to grow and very soon she's going to be a big threat," he said.
"It's the biggest day of my life," Klochkova said. "However, I wasn't nervous or afraid being in the same race as the Olympic champion."

Olympic silver medallist Sandra Voelker just held off the challenge of fast-finishing Martina Moravcova of Slovakia to win the women's 100 metres freestyle and give Germany the first pool swimming title of the 12-day championships.
Voelker won by just 0.08 seconds in 55.38. "I felt very uncomfortable with the hot sun on my back," she said. "If conditions had been much cooler I could have swum much faster."

Alexander Goukov of Belarus won a desperately close men's 100 metres breaststroke, edging 1988 Olympic silver medallist Karoly Guttler of Hungary into second place by 0.06 seconds, with Czech Daniel Malek a mere 0.04 seconds further back.
Olympic champion Frederik DeBurghgraeve of Belgium did not defend his title.

Britain's Paul Palmer, silver medallist at the 1995 European championships in the 400 freestyle, went one better and won the gold in the men's 200 freestyle when he forged past Italy's Massimiliano Rosolino on the final length.
Palmer won in 1:48.85, with Rosolino second in 1:49.02.
"I never really thought in the build-up that I would get silver or any other medal than gold," Palmer said.
"I thought 'if I'm up with them at 100 I'll definitely win'."
